results.title: KV Cache Management
results.content:
InfiniGen's KV cache management provides advantages over alternative approaches:

1.   Full KV Cache (Baseline): Stores all KV pairs in GPU memory, limited by available memory.

2.   H2O: Offloads KV cache to host memory, but still requires transferring the full cache.

3.   Quantization: Reduces precision of KV cache entries, trading accuracy for memory efficiency.

Sources: README.md

## Integration with Overall System [...] 1.   Memory Footprint: The KV cache grows linearly with sequence length, consuming substantial GPU memory.
2.   Host-Device Transfers: In offloading-based systems, transferring the entire KV cache between host and GPU memory creates bottlenecks.
3.   Inefficient Memory Usage: Not all cached tokens contribute equally to generating the next token.

Sources: README.md

# KV Cache Management

Relevant source files
   README.md

This document details the dynamic Key-Value (KV) Cache Management system in InfiniGen, which is a core component responsible for reducing memory footprint during LLM inference while maintaining model performance. The KV Cache Management works in conjunction with the Token Speculation Mechanism that identifies important tokens and the Prefetching System that retrieves essential KV cache entries.

results.content:
Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive performance across various natural language processing tasks. Serving LLM inference for generating long contents, however, poses a challenge due to the enormous memory footprint of the transient state, known as the key-value (KV) cache, which scales with the sequence length and batch size. In this paper, we present InfiniGen, a novel KV cache management framework tailored for long-text generation, which synergistically works [...] View Paper
snu-comparch/InfiniGen

## AI Overview

When an LLM generates long text, it stores keys and values from earlier tokens so it need not recompute them. This store is the KV cache, and it grows with sequence length and batch size. Offloading the cache from GPU to larger CPU memory helps fit the workload. However, fetching it back over the CPU–GPU connection can become a major inference cost. [...] InfiniGen predicts from the immediately preceding layer. For OPT-13B, measured on a random 2,000-token PG-19 sentence, the authors report an average cosine similarity of 0.96 between adjacent Transformer-block inputs across layers. The paper notes that inputs to distant layers differ.
